prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No trip planner spreads visitors across seasons and places at scale, so the Main KPI of 1,000,000,000 trips planned with crowd-spreading is unmet. Destination measures are fees and booking systems, not planners: Venice charged a EUR 5 to 10 access fee on 54 days in 2025 and still saw about 25,000 paying visitors on peak days (https://www.lonelyplanet.com/news/venice-introduces-new-booking-system-and-entry-fee-for-visitors). Google Maps shows popular times and area busyness but does not recommend alternative destinations to relieve hotspots (https://www.entrepreneur.com/business-news/google-will-tell-you-how-crowded-places-are-in-real-time/285582). Booking.com's AI Trip Planner builds itineraries without documented seasonality steering, though 42 percent of its surveyed travellers plan off-peak (https://www.hospitalitynet.org/news/4117122.html). Research on congestion-aware tourism recommenders relies on simulations, surveys and focus groups, with few field measurements of crowd reduction (https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-58839-6_35). Honest limit: general AI trip planners and crowd displays are known answers; measured redistribution of real visitor flows is open, and it depends on platforms UAIN does not control.
